# Releasing

Releases are cut by the [Release workflow](workflows/release.yml). Nothing needs
to be bumped, tagged or written by hand.

## Cutting a release

1. Make sure everything you want to ship is merged into `main` and that **Lint**,
   **Hassfest** and **Validate** were green on the pull requests that landed it.
   Those workflows do not run on pushes to `main` — if you want to confirm the
   branch itself before releasing, run each from **Actions → Run workflow**
   against `main`.
2. Go to **Actions → Release → Run workflow**.
3. Choose the bump:
   - **patch** — bug fixes (`0.24.0` → `0.24.1`)
   - **minor** — new shade types, new entities, new features (`0.24.0` → `0.25.0`)
   - **major** — breaking changes, e.g. requiring users to reconfigure
4. Optionally give it a **title**. Left blank it uses the version number;
   a one-line summary of the change reads better in the releases list.
5. Tick **prerelease** to ship it to beta testers only — see below.
6. Tick **draft** if you want to rewrite the notes before users see it.

The workflow bumps `version` in
[manifest.json](../custom_components/hunterdouglas_powerview_ble/manifest.json),
commits it as `chore: bump version to X.Y.Z`, tags that commit `vX.Y.Z`, and
creates the GitHub release with notes generated from the PRs and commits since
the last one.

Unlike the sibling `ha_google_weather` repo, the version lives in **one** place
here — `const.py` carries no `VERSION` constant, so there is nothing to keep in
lockstep.

HACS picks the release up from that point. Because the tag points at the bump
commit, the version HACS installs always matches the tag.

## The first release

This repository has no tags yet, and neither did upstream, so there is no tag
history to collide with. The manifest sits at `0.24.0` (normalised from
upstream's two-part `0.24`), which means the first run of the workflow produces
`0.24.1`, `0.25.0` or `1.0.0` depending on the bump you pick.

Until that first release exists, HACS installs this integration from the default
branch and cannot offer users update notifications — which is the main thing a
maintained fork should provide. Cut one early.

## Pre-releases

Ticking **prerelease** changes one thing: GitHub flags the release as a
pre-release and it is not marked *latest*. HACS only offers a pre-release to
users who have turned on beta versions for this repository (in HACS, open
**Hunter Douglas PowerView (BLE) → ⋮ → Redownload**, then enable **Show beta
versions**). Everyone else keeps seeing the previous stable release and is never
prompted.

This matters more here than in most repos: the maintainer owns hardwired shades
only and cannot test battery-powered behaviour locally, so changes touching
battery SoC, the charging sensor or the hub's battery-powered flag are worth
shipping as a pre-release first.

The version number is a normal `X.Y.Z` — there is no `-beta` suffix. A
pre-release of `0.25.0` *is* `0.25.0`, in the tag and in `manifest.json`, so
promoting it later needs no new build:

> Open the release on GitHub → **Edit** → untick **Set as a pre-release**, tick
> **Set as the latest release** → **Update release**.

HACS then offers it to everyone, running byte-identical code to what the beta
testers were on. No second version, tag, commit or set of release notes.

If the beta turns out to be broken instead, just fix it and cut the next one.
`main` is already bumped, so the workflow will offer the following patch next —
version numbers spent on abandoned betas are simply skipped, which costs
nothing.

## Notes

- The release notes are generated by GitHub from merged pull request titles, so
  descriptive PR titles produce a usable changelog for free. A published
  release's notes can still be edited on GitHub afterwards.
- HACS shows these notes in Home Assistant's update dialog cumulatively, across
  every release between the user's installed version and the latest, so they
  need to read well standalone.
- Generated notes cover everything since the *previous tag*, and an abandoned
  pre-release still leaves a tag behind. So if `0.25.0` is cut as a beta and
  then dropped, `0.25.1`'s notes describe only what changed after `0.25.0` — the
  beta's own changes are not repeated. Worth editing the notes by hand in that
  case.
- The workflow refuses to run from anything other than `main`, refuses to
  overwrite a tag that already exists, and refuses to run if the manifest
  version is not `X.Y.Z`.
- If it fails partway, nothing is half-published: the bump commit and the tag
  are pushed with `git push --atomic`, so both land or neither does.
